notes.decision: Translated 'heaven-bearers' as the natural reference of 'foremost of all (the) X' applied to the Pillar of Glory / Perfect Man, who in Manichaean cosmology is the chief of the Omophoroi (Atlas-figures). Probable analysis: ⲃⲁⲓ̈- 'bearer' (from ϥⲁⲓ 'lift, bear') + -ⲉⲡⲓⲱ as obscure plural-marker or compound-element for the burden borne (heaven/cosmos). Cf. accumulated ⲡⲥⲟⲩⲓⲧ 'unique upholder of all the omophoroi.'

Lyc. ⲭⲡⲟ here understood as 'set, place, establish' applied to ⲣⲉⲧϥ̄ 'his foot' — 'he set his foot from below to above.' Likely Lyc. variant of ϫⲡⲟ 'produce, set forth' or related to ⲧⲁⲍⲟ 'set' (within the lacuna's range). Spatial 'from below to above' fits the Pillar's cosmic-bearing function.

ⲧⲱⲃⲥ rendered 'sting/prick/needle' (fits parallel verbal occurrence in line 21 ⲁϥⲧⲱⲃⲥ ⲛ̄ⲧⲛⲟⲩⲛⲉ 'he stung the root'); ⲡϩⲟⲩ tentatively 'the rear/back' (Lyc. for ⲡⲁϩⲟⲩ) — i.e., the back-portion of the death-storehouse. Alternative reading 'the evil one's storehouse' (taking ⲡϩⲟⲩ = ⲡⲉⲑⲟⲟⲩ 'the evil') is also possible.

Triple-verb cosmic-conquest sequence: ϩⲱⲙ 'press, tread upon'; ⲗⲱⲙⲥ 'submerge' (or 'defile'; cf. accumulated ⲗⲱⲗⲙ̄ⲥ 'defile'); ⲧⲱⲃⲥ 'stamp, prick.' Object 'root of death' (ⲛⲧⲛⲟⲩⲛⲉ ⲛⲧⲉ ⲡⲙⲟⲩ) supports physical-conquest reading over defile-reading.

'The Glorious One' (in glossary) — title of Jesus here functioning as the cosmic agent who summons the Great Thought (= the third rock = the Holy Church indwelt). Note that Jesus the Glorious is summoner here (not the Third Ambassador as in line 12), preserving the precise dual-summoner structure of the kephalaion.

Cognate-object construction: 'she stands-fast in a standing-fast.' Both forms from ⲧⲱⲕ ⲁⲣⲉⲧ⸗ idiom (in glossary). The fem. ending -ⲥ vs masc. -ϥ alternation in the same idiom is unusual; possibly a fixed nominal form ⲧⲱⲕ ⲁⲣⲉⲧϥ̄ functions as substantive 'standing-fast' modified by ⲙⲙⲏⲉ 'true.'

Lines 6 and 30 contain bare chapter-numeral markers (62, 63) functioning as headers within the manuscript layout, distinct from the full chapter-titles in lines 7 and 31. Preserved as separate segments to honor the scribal structure.
